narrative:
The model estimates a 58% chance that you will leave your current role, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors that, in combination, signal a higher risk of departure compared to colleagues who are expected to stay.

The strongest influence is that you have received other job opportunities while at the company. Most employees predicted to stay (77%) have not received such offers, so this factor pushes the prediction noticeably toward leaving. 

Your 11+ years of overall professional experience is the second most important reason. While this is valuable, only 15% of employees expected to stay have this much experience. The model sees very experienced staff as more likely to explore external options, so this also pulls the outcome toward leaving.

Finally, you find balancing work and personal life difficult. Only 9% of those predicted to stay report the same struggle. This challenge further increases the predicted likelihood of departure.

Taken together, these three elements outweigh many positive aspects of your profile, such as your PhD, high emotional commitment, strong recognition, and satisfaction with your job and environment.

The organization should discuss retention strategies with you, particularly around work-life support and career growth. You may wish to reflect on whether the external opportunities align better with your long-term goals. Addressing the work-life balance issue could benefit both sides.
